ingredients.item: salmon fillets , skin on, pin bones pulled, room temperature
Steamed rice , sesame-soy cucumber , perilla leaves

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: Skin-down on the moderate zone, oiled grate, 5–6 minutes undisturbed — the skin crisps in its own rendered fat exactly the way the duck skin does in #M19, and the skin is the platform: pull the fillet early elsewhere but never on the skin.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the skin releases clean and crisp-gold at the edges; the flesh at the sides has turned opaque a third of the way up the fillet.

instructions.heading: Step 2
instructions.action: Flip once, 2 minutes on the flesh side, then the glaze: brush, 45 seconds, second thin brush-stroke, and pull at the table's preferred center — salmon's window is wide, from just-translucent at 50 °C to opaque-flaky at 58 °C, and this glaze suits the juicier end.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: a test flake at the thick end: it parts along the grain with no force, still glossy inside, glaze set brick-tacky on the outside. If the glaze blackens, the hot zone ran past its sugar — the fish is fine underneath; notch the fire down for the second set.

instructions.heading: Step 3
instructions.action: Sesame and scallion over, platter with the cucumber banchan and perilla beside.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: eating test: glaze edge, salmon's sweet fat, the cucumber's cold snap between bites — rich, spiced, reset. A piece of the crisp skin with the glaze is the record's best single bite, and the cook's by right.

storageNotes: Raw fillets keep 1 day; the glaze keeps a week refrigerated and improves. Cooked, 2 days — cold flaked salmon over rice with the last of the glaze thinned as a sauce.

Variations: the doenjang-glaze fork for the mellower table (#SF11); the same glaze on the black cod at its slower clock; broiler path — skin-down on a sheet pan, top rack, glaze in the last 3 minutes — for the no-grill weeknight.
